title: Bounded walk computation
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $B$ be a natural number, and let $\sigma=(p,n,a,b,s,t,tmp,st,nx)$ be a nine-register state. Suppose $2|x|+2\le B$, every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $s<n$, $t<n$, $st\le n$, and $2n+2+2n^2\le |x|$. Define a directed edge relation on the natural numbers by declaring $u$ adjacent to $v$ when the bit of $x$ at position $2n+2+2(un+v)$ is true, with out-of-range entries treated as false. Then the program started at label $w0$ in state $\sigma$ terminates on every branch with all registers at most $B$, and has an accepting branch exactly when there is a walk from $s$ to $t$ of length at most $n-st$.
hypotheses_covered: Every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a finite bit string and let $B$ be a natural number with $2|x|+2\le B$. Let
$\sigma$ be a nine-register configuration whose register values are all at most $B$.
Suppose its source $s$ and target $t$ are both less than its vertex count $n$, its step
count $st$ is at most $n$, and $|x|\ge 2n+2+2n^2$. Regard $x$ as encoding a directed
graph on vertices $0,\ldots,n-1$, with an edge from $u$ to $v$ when the bit at position
$2n+2+2(un+v)$ is $1$. Then the program started at label $w0$ with configuration
$\sigma$ terminates on every branch with all register values bounded by $B$, and has an
accepting branch exactly when there is a walk from $s$ to $t$ of length at most $n-st$
in this graph.
